weeklyQuote: ChatGPT Wallet will make jewellers sell to software before they ever meet the buyer.
editorialTake:
France and Botswana are drawing a clear line on diamond names as lab-grown stones win bridal sales. The countries signed the Paris Declaration on Natural Diamonds, reserving the word “diamond” for natural stones.

Lab-grown diamonds lead engagement sales at many jewellers, according to INSTORE’s 2026 Big Survey. Buyers use the savings to choose bigger stones within the same budget.

For bridal jewellers, the declaration gives different labels to products competing for the same spending. A switch to lab-grown stones can change what a jeweller sells without cutting what the buyer spends.

readOneThing.title: Amazon's plan to own the world's product data and fight AI shopping agents

items.title: Amazon's plan to own the world's product data and fight AI shopping agents
bullets: Amazon has drafted plans for World Product Graph, a database covering products worldwide, including items it does not sell.
Coca-Cola and Bayer have signed up to supply product data, according to an internal document reviewed by Reuters.
The document gives an aspirational release date of October 1, 2027, but Amazon said it does not necessarily reflect current plans.
items.summary: Amazon plans to collect data on virtually every product sold worldwide through World Product Graph, including items it does not stock.

items.title: Richemont Looks to the Future After Posting Double-Digit Growth in First-Half Sales, Profits
bullets: Richemont reported sales of 12.3 billion euros and operating profit of 3.1 billion euros for the six months through September 30.
Jewelry sales rose 18 percent to 9.15 billion euros, while specialist watch sales increased 9 percent to 1.71 billion euros.
Anton Rupert was confirmed as non-executive co-deputy chairman, while his father Johann said he had no plans to retire.
items.summary: Richemont posted double-digit first-half sales and profit growth, while chairman Johann Rupert said he has no plans to retire.

items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns From Nvidia After Affairs
bullets: Nvidia named finance chief Colette Kress interim chief executive after Jensen Huang resigned following revelations about affairs with a subordinate and an alleged Chinese spy.
The board appointed longtime technology investor Harvey Jones chairman and said it would consider internal and external candidates for permanent chief executive.
Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for chips used in major artificial intelligence projects.
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive amid scrutiny over affairs; finance chief Colette Kress was named interim leader.

items.title: Richemont Sales Climb 16% in H1 With All Regions, Except for the Middle East, Showing Robust Growth
bullets: Richemont reported first-half sales of 12.3 billion euros, with jewelry sales growing faster than its watch and fashion businesses.
Operating profit rose 33 percent to 3.1 billion euros despite higher raw material costs, particularly for gold.
Chief executive Nicolas Bos said local customers accounted for most purchases, with tourists generating around 15 percent of sales.
items.summary: Richemont’s first-half sales rose 17% at constant exchange rates to €12.3 billion, with double-digit growth in every region except the Middle East.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, allowing its 'dots' AI agents to make purchases for users
bullets: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet on Friday for U.S. Pro subscribers over 18, requiring a security check for every purchase.
Payment networks provide card details specific to each transaction, keeping users' actual card information hidden from OpenAI's agents.
United Airlines said Wednesday it would block AI agents from booking tickets, while Amazon already prevents them from purchasing products.
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, letting its AI agents make purchases for users while cardholders keep their existing credit card rewards.

items.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in stock market flotation
bullets: Anthropic filed plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, with trading expected to begin next week.
Anthropic reported annual revenue running at $81 billion as of 31 October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
The company has committed more than $70 billion to computing purchases and leases over the next 12 months.
items.summary: Anthropic is seeking a stock market valuation of up to $1.4tn, below the previously reported $2tn target as investors question the AI boom.

items.title: Phillips Sets Another Record With the Highest-Grossing Watch Auction in History
bullets: Phillips sold all 217 lots for $112.3 million at its Geneva watch auction on November 7 and 8.
An F.P. Journe Chronomètre à Résonance “Régence” sold for $10.6 million, leading 13 Journe watches totaling $38.9 million.
Phillips has further watch auctions scheduled in Hong Kong in late November and New York in early December.
items.summary: Phillips’ Geneva watch auction raised $112.3 million, the highest total in watch auction history, setting 24 world records over two days.

items.title: Fire, fines and a costly comeback: Coupang’s long road back to profit
bullets: Coupang reported a third-quarter operating loss of US$450 million as revenue rose 7 per cent to US$9.96 billion.
Coupang’s active Korean retail customers reached 25.2 million, exceeding levels before the data breach that exposed information linked to 33.7 million accounts.
Coupang is building warehouses ahead of demand in Taiwan, where paid membership more than doubled from a year earlier.
items.summary: Coupang’s results show momentum, with no clear timeline for a return to profit.
